purpose: samarpitaṃ: the copy was written and offered/dedicated by the scribe himself; recipient not named
notes: Only one person named. Maheśvarānanda is styled mahābuddhopāsaka (written mahāvuddhopāśaka), i.e. a Buddhist lay devotee, and 'of Lalitapura' (Patan); the genitive is attached to the scribe, so Lalitapura is strictly his residence and only by inference the place of copying. 'likhitaṃ samarpitaṃ' implies he both wrote and donated/dedicated the copy, hence the added donor role. Date: three-digit saṃvat 959 with Nepali 'sāla miti' = NS 959, Pauṣa kṛṣṇa 5, Friday, c. Dec 1838/Jan 1839 CE. Matches the catalogue fields (scribe Maheśvarānaṃda, NS 959). Śrīkaṇṭhanātha in the title formula is a deity, not listed. No author, king or beneficiary named. Textual corruptions: nirṇao, śukravāa, paṭala (!) for paṭalaḥ, mahāvuddhopāśaka for mahābuddhopāsaka.
